text:
alex: thinking aloud — we keep hitting message-attribute limits and 20+ headers when a request fans out to workers. proposal: a single compact header ("trace_cookie") that carries minimal trace context + an opaque token to rehydrate full span payload if needed.

maria: love the idea, fewer headers would help nginx + gRPC. what's inside the cookie?

alex: sketch: v1|base64(payload)|hmac. payload = {tp, td, sampled, delta_spans, bag:maybe}. base64 to avoid weird chars. hmac to prevent tamper.

samir: two quick concerns: (1) queue/message attribute size limits vary across providers, (2) retries/delayed visibility — cookie TTL needs to survive resubmits.

jun: can we instead put a short opaque key in the cookie that points at a small KV store (ephemeral) with the full context? then queue only carries the key. cost+operational tradeoffs though.

alex: yep that was one option I had: either embed enough to reconstruct (no remote lookup) OR embed a key + rely on a short-lived store. hybrid suggestion: embed minimal routing fields (traceparent + sampling + first-parent-id) inline and optional key for full details when callers opt-in.

maria: for the inline case, we should pick a minimal carrier shape that maps cleanly to W3C traceparent + baggage. i.e. don't try to shove spans. just enough to stitch.

samir: also: when we rehydrate big spans we must be careful about retention windows for the KV store. if a message sits in a delayed queue for an hour we need at least that ttl + safety. that costs money if lots of messages.

jun: what if we sign the payload and store it in the message body itself (encrypted) instead of a global KV? that avoids central lookup but increases message size. might break providers that disallow large attributes but body is usually okay.

alex: true. body vs attribute tradeoff varies. we should treat gateways differently: gateway->worker synchronous path can carry trace headers normally; async fanout path uses cookie. also need a deterministic reconstructor in workers.

maria: operational note: exporters downstream (tempo/jaeger) will see split spans unless we propagate a stable parent id and a minimal timestamp. we must guarantee id/correlation so traces stitch.

samir: sampling semantics matter: if initial request was sampled=false, do we still carry full context? probably only minimal to avoid creating noise. sample decisions should be portable and honored by rehydration.

jun: edge case: cross-region when rehydration hits a central KV in another region — latency and failure modes. maybe store with region affinity or allow fallback to embedded minimal context.

alex: implementation plan suggestion: 1) spec cookie v1: fields = traceparent, sampled, root_ts, parent_delta (optional), kv_key (optional), sig. encoding = base64(json) + hex(sig). 2) gateway libs implement composer/decomposer. 3) worker lib tries local decode -> if kv_key present try KV -> fallback to embedded. 4) expose flags in console to show rehydrate failures in trace diagnostics.

maria: can we add a debug flag to surface when rehydrate fell back to minimal so we can measure how often full context is lost? :eyes:

samir: +1. we'll want metrics: rehydrate_success, rehydrate_miss, expired_token. also track avg rehydration latency.

jun: security: HMAC prevents tamper but not replay. add ttl and optionally nonce. KV entries are single-use tokens maybe.

alex: good point. single-use tokens reduce replay but complicate retries. maybe allow idempotent tokens vs single-use depending on queue semantics.

otel-bot: reminder: there is an existing RFC in google drive: "async-trace-cookie-proposal-v0" (link) — please update with the v1 fields before EOD.

maria: I'll take the RFC edit. samir you okay to prototype KV-backed rehydrate and metrics? jun can you spike region-affine storage options? alex will draft composer/decomposer with example code.

samir: yep, I'll start a small TTL KV backed by our Redis cluster and simulate delayed retries.

jun: I'll check multi-region options (redis cluster vs signed JWT payload).

alex: initial code sample for header composer (rough):

```
// compose trace_cookie
const payload = { tp: traceparent, s: sampled, rt: Date.now(), p: parentId }
const b = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(payload)).toString('base64')
const sig = HMAC(secret, b)
return `trace_cookie: v1|${b}|${sig}`
```

maria: perfect. let's sync on the RFC edits and then we can try a controlled rollout on a non-critical gateway. canary to 5% traffic. :thumbsup:

alex: SGTM. thanks all — will post a PR for the composer/decomposer and link the RFC.

otel-bot: ticket created: TE-4213 "trace_cookie v1 RFC"
